newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Mystery corpse found on Russian aircraft carrier.
newsitem.headline: Mystery corpse found on Russian aircraft carrier.

text.p: The three-year-old corpse of an unknown person who apparently committed suicide has been found aboard a Russian aircraft carrier, officials said on Friday.
The body was discovered in a ventilation shaft on the Admiral Kuznetsov, flagship of the Northern Fleet and Russia's only working aircraft carrier.
It had lain unnoticed because of the huge size of the ship, an official from the fleet's press office said by telephone.

"We believe he was a suicide victim because we found a message on the wall of the shaft saying 'I am leaving the world of my own free will'," said a spokesman for naval prosecutors investigating the case.
"Most likely the body was one of the specialists who do repairs and maintenance on the fleet," he added.
The navy thought at first it might have been one of the crew. "But a detailed check showed that none of the crew had ever gone missing," the press official said.

A theory that a shipbuilding worker had fallen into the shaft during construction was dropped after pathologists established that the corpse had been in the ventilation shaft for no longer than three years. The carrier was built in January 1991.
The Admiral Kuznetsov has 1,500 crew and more than 30 km (20 miles) of rooms and corridors.
"There are more than 2,000 rooms with various functions and many are very rarely inspected by the crew," said the official from the fleet.
He said two sailors from the same village had served on the ship for two years without meeting once.
